answer: A new agent, call it juniper, cannot simply mint a thousand identities, because joining requires locking a refundable stake that is slashed if peers prove duplicate behaviour. Every action leaves a public thread of signed attestations, so a second identity cannot hide: its history either stays empty and untrusted, or it copies the first and the overlap is detected. Trusted work earns an onyx credential that only accumulates slowly through verified tasks, so buying many cheap identities never buys the reputation that gates valuable work.
